programme.title: An Art Lovers' Guide
programme.desc: Bordering the Caspian Sea, Baku offers a tantalising mix of the ancient and modern - at the crossroads of east meets west, on the ancient silk trading route. It is also an authoritarian state, where cultural life is tightly controlled.

programme.title: Britain's Lost Masterpieces
programme.desc: Bendor Grosvenor and Emma Dabiri visit Brighton Museum to investigate who painted two neglected pictures of religious subjects. Bendor believes a grubby image of Mary Magdalene repenting her sins may be by a forgotten master of Francesco Trevisani.

programme.title: Earth's Natural Wonders
programme.desc: In many of the world's most extraordinary natural wonders there is an abundance of animals. These can be a devastating threat to the people who live there, or they can provide a means of survival, but often at a high price.

programme.title: Earth's Natural Wonders
programme.desc: In some natural wonders people push themselves to the limit to survive. For the people who call these extraordinary places home, survival requires skill, ingenuity and bravery. These places include Brazil, Ethiopia, Laos and Switzerland.

programme.title: The Good Life
programme.desc: Tom and Barbara feel sorry for Jerry when they discover that, despite the jodhpurs and the hacking jacket, Margo isn't going riding twice a week as she claims. Is she having an affair?

programme.title: Yes, Minister
programme.desc: Jim Hacker finds himself in possession of some embarrassing information regarding the sale of British arms to terrorist groups. This all sounds strangely familiar.

programme.title: Oh, Doctor Beeching!
programme.desc: Staff worry about Beeching's cuts. Harry's turkey Oscar escapes, halting a train. Cecil calls a meeting about lax behaviour. May dislikes Cecil's new pompous manner. Jack suspects Cecil and May's past connection, but Ethel dismisses his concerns.

programme.title: Dad's Army
programme.desc: It occurs to Captain Mainwaring that much of the valuable time of his unit is taken up with non-combatant activities such as button sewing, brass polishing and office duties. He discusses with Sergeant Wilson a scheme to recruit some women members.

programme.title: The Signalman
programme.desc: Near a tunnel, a traveller encounters a fearful signalman. Puzzled by the worker's odd behaviour, he reassures him and enters the signal box. There, the signalman begins to unfold an extraordinary tale that will captivate the traveller.

programme.title: Murder on the Victorian Railway
programme.desc: London 1864. On a Hackney bound train, a guard discovers blood in a first class carriage - and a body on the railway embankment. For the first time, a murder has taken place on Britain's railways. Over a hundred years later, this documentary uses the first hand testimony of the people involved at the time to explore this unique event and how it provoked a huge public outcry and debate.

programme.title: Timeshift
programme.sub-title: The Joy of (Train) Sets: The Model Railway Story
programme.desc: From Hornby to Triang and beyond, this documentary explores how the British have been in love with model railways for more than a century.

programme.title: Timeshift
programme.sub-title: The Engine That Powers the World
programme.desc: The surprising story of the hidden powerhouse behind the globalised world - the diesel engine, a 19th-century invention that has become indispensable to the 21st. It's a turtle versus hare tale in which the diesel engine races the petrol engine in a competition to replace ageing steam technology - a race eventually won hands down by diesel. Car enthusiast presenter Mark Evans gets excitedly hands on with some of the many applications of Mr Diesel's original creation.

programme.title: Timeshift
programme.desc: The surprising story of how Britain entered a new age of steam railways after the Second World War and why it quickly came to an end. After the war, the largely-destroyed railways of Europe were rebuilt to carry more modern diesel and electric trains. Britain, however, chose to build thousands of brand new steam locomotives. Did we stay with steam because coal was seen as the most reliable power source or were the railways run by men who couldn't bear to let go of their beloved steam trains?

programme.title: Great Railway Journeys
programme.sub-title: Crewe to Crewe With Victoria Wood
programme.desc: Victoria Wood makes a round trip to the north of Britain from Crewe, taking in both the east and west coasts. On her way north she visits Carnforth station, location of the classic film `Brief Encounter', takes the North West Regional Railways service across Morecambe Bay to Barrow and the Cumbrian Coastal line to Carlisle before reaching Thurso, the most northerly point possible by train.

programme.title: London to Brighton Side by Side
programme.desc: In 1953 the BBC made a point-of-view film from the London to Brighton train. In 1983 they did the same again. This is a film made of both runs at once with every bridge, siding, tunnel and station running side by side in unlikely synchronisation.

programme.title: Great Railway Journeys
programme.desc: Michael Palin, a keen train spotter when young, fulfils his boyhood dream of travelling length of the country from Euston to Kyle of Lochalsh.

programme.title: Phil Davis Remembers...The Firm
programme.desc: Phil Davis pays tribute to maverick director Alan Clarke as he looks back on his time filming the 1989 made-for-television film `The Firm'. Phil recalls how he was cast in the role as the sleek, villainous 'Yeti'.

programme.title: Screen Two
programme.desc: Drama about Bex, an estate agent with an apparently respectable family life who is also a football hooligan leading of a vicious 'firm' of thugs who are determined to lead a national hooligan assault on Europe.

programme.title: Why the Industrial Revolution Happened Here
programme.desc: Professor Jeremy Black examines the Industrial Revolution. He explains the unique economic, social and political conditions that by the 19th century, led to Britain becoming the richest, most powerful nation on Earth.

programme.title: Steam Days
programme.desc: Miles Kington experiences the power of a London, Midland & Scottish Railway (LMS) Stanier `Black Five' on a journey from Fort William across the western Highlands via Glenfinnan to Mallaig.

programme.title: The Train Now Departing
programme.desc: An examination of events surrounding the proposed closure of the Settle to Carlisle line, one of the most magnificent stretches of railway line in England, over 72 miles long and England's highest mainline.

programme.title: Brief Encounter
programme.desc: Housewife Laura Jesson meets Dr Alec Harvey at a railway station cafe and there is a spark between them. They are tempted to adultery before they realise their marriages are more important than the fleeting happiness they may find together.

programme.title: Sarah Churchwell Remembers... The Great Gatsby
programme.desc: Sarah Churchwell looks at the origins of `The Great Gatsby', F Scott Fitzgerald's evocative novel of the Roaring Twenties, and the inspiration behind its plot and characters.

programme.title: The Great Gatsby
programme.desc: At the centre of the story is Jay Gatsby, whose lust for money and power conceals a deeper passion, his love for Daisy, the woman he met in his early youth but lost to the bullying but wealthy Tom Buchanan. His millions made, Gatsby moves into a mansion close to Daisy, where he holds lavish parties, hoping to win her back.

programme.title: Omnibus
programme.sub-title: The Great Gatsby: Midnight in Manhattan
programme.desc: A profile from 2000 of writer F Scott Fitzgerald on the seventy-fifth anniversary of the publication of `The Great Gatsby'. Is it merely 'an entertaining anecdote' or should it be seen as 'the most important novel of the twentieth century'?

programme.title: Tár
programme.desc: Renowned musician Lydia Tár is days away from recording the symphony that will elevate her career. When all elements seem to conspire against her, Lydia's adopted daughter Petra becomes an integral emotional support for her struggling mother.

programme.title: Talking Business
programme.desc: For more than two decades Google has dominated the way we search, shop and do business online - so how is AI changing all of that? We hear from the digital marketing guru Sir Martin Sorrel and the boss of Algolia which handles the second biggest number of searches in the world. Plus from fish fingers to ice creams we catch up with the CEO of Europe's biggest frozen food empire Nomad foods.
